records.issue_text: In-place ImageMagick convert with from == to on the uploaded tempfile can truncate/corrupt the file; the unchecked false return causes retries against a corrupted file and broken uploads
records.rationale: The new upload resize loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, i.e., it runs ImageMagick conversion in-place with `from == to` on the uploaded tempfile. `OptimizedImage.optimize` delegates to `convert_with(instructions, to)`, which can return `false` on failure, but the controller ignores the return value and just decrements `attempt`, potentially retrying on an already-modified/corrupted tempfile and then proceeding to `Upload.create_for(...)` with whatever is left. This matches the finding’s risk of truncation/corruption plus unchecked failure during re

records.issue_text: Downsizing runs on the request thread inside create_upload with no timeout budget; five sequential ImageMagick invocations can block a worker and hit web-server timeout (502)
records.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the diff adds an inline loop that can run up to 5 times on the request path: `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` then `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` (synchronous image processing). `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes a shell command via backticks (ImageMagick) with no timeout/budget shown. This creates a concrete risk of tying up a web worker during sequential external process invocations, potentially leading to request timeouts (e.g., 502) under load or with slow conversion
records.stripped_text: Downsizing runs on the request thread inside create_upload with no timeout budget; five sequential ImageMagick invocations can block a worker and hit web-server timeout (502)

records.issue_text: FileHelper.download hardcodes download cap at 10MB while the downsizing feature exists to accept larger images, silently excluding the API/URL upload path from the feature
records.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API/URL path now downloads with a hard cap of `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). The newly added downsizing loop only runs after a `tempfile` is obtained, so any image larger than 10MB can never reach the downsizing logic and will fail/return nil on download. This creates a real limitation specifically for the URL/API upload path that undermines the “upload large images then reduce to allowed size” behavior added just below.

records.issue_text: Hardcoded 10MB cap in utilities.js:182 replaces the per-type site setting (max_${type}_size_kb), silently removing the attachment size limit for non-image upload types that are never downsized server-side
records.rationale: The diff clearly replaces the configurable per-type client-side size check `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in `utilities.js`, and also hardcodes `maxSizeKB` to 10MB for the 413 error path. This removes/ignores the per-type site setting for upload size limits on the client, which can cause incorrect behavior vs configured limits (e.g., allowing uploads larger than the configured limit or blocking uploads when the configured limit is >10MB), particularly for non-image types that are not covered by the new server-side downsize logic added i
